raw_text:
Below is a safe, progressive 12-week strength program for your advanced lifter at 20 weeks pregnant. It respects: no supine work after week 16, no max attempts, no contact sports. The emphasis is submaximal strength maintenance, posture, pelvic floor function, and joint-friendly training as body mechanics change. Three strength days per week plus one optional low-impact conditioning/mobility day. Each session is ~45–60 minutes.

Global guidance and safety
- Intensity/auto-regulation: Use RPE 6–7 most of the time (2–4 reps in reserve). Never exceed RPE 8. No Valsalva; exhale through the sticking point.
- Positions: Avoid supine and prolonged prone. Favor standing, seated, half-/tall-kneeling, side-lying, or incline 30–45°.
- Core: Avoid high intra-abdominal pressure moves (max bracing, heavy front planks, sit-ups, toes-to-bar). Favor breathing-based core, anti-rotation, quadruped, side-lying, carries.
- Hinge and squat: Maintain patterns with reduced ROM as belly grows (e.g., blocks for deadlift, box for squats). Consider safety bar/front-loaded squats for torso position.
- Balance and joint care: Relaxin increases laxity—use hand support for split stance, step-ups, and single-leg work. Reduce impact/bounding.
- Stop immediately and contact OB if any red flags: vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, dizziness/fainting, chest pain, severe headache, calf pain/swelling, regular painful contractions, shortness of breath before exertion, decreased fetal movement.
- Warm-up every session (8–10 min): 
  - 3–5 min easy cardio (bike/rower/treadmill walk)
  - 360° breath + pelvic floor coordination: 5–6 slow breaths (inhale: expand ribs/belly/pelvis; exhale: gentle pelvic floor lift; then fully relax)
  - Dynamic mobility: cat-cow x8, tall-kneel T-spine rotations x6/side, 90/90 hip switches x8, band pull-aparts x12, bodyweight squats x10
- Cool-down (5–8 min): Easy walking + side-lying or seated breathing, gentle hip flexor/calf stretches. Avoid deep end-range holds >30s.
- Diastasis-friendly cues: Watch for doming/peaking or coning; regress (elevate hands, lighten load, shorten lever) if present.
- Accessories/substitutions: Where barbells feel uncomfortable, swap to dumbbells/cables/machines.

Program structure
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week (A, B, C). Optional Day D: low-impact conditioning/mobility 20–30 min.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Solidify pregnancy-safe variations, establish RPE, small progressions.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Maintain strength with slight variation, tempo/pauses for stimulus without heavy loading.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Reduce axial load, prioritize comfort, range control, and movement quality heading into third trimester.

Key exercise menu (used throughout)
- Squat patterns: Safety bar squat or front squat; goblet box squat (later).
- Hinge patterns: Trap bar deadlift from 2–4" blocks; DB/KB RDL; cable pull-through; sumo KB deadlift.
- Upper push: Incline DB press (30–45°), standing cable chest press, half-kneeling landmine press, elevated push-up to rack bar/box.
- Upper pull: Seated cable row, 1-arm cable row, TRX row (foot position adjusts intensity), lat pulldown or assisted pull-up.
- Core/carries: Pallof press/holds, anti-rotation chops, bird dog, side plank variations, suitcase/farmer carries.
- Lower accessory/glute: Supported split squat, step-up, B-stance RDL, lateral band walks, cable kickbacks.
- Conditioning finisher options: Sled push, incline walk, fan bike intervals—moderate, conversational pace.

Progression notes
- Progress weekly if last set ≤RPE 7: add 1–2% load or 1 rep as indicated.
- If any movement approaches RPE 8 or technique degrades, hold or reduce 5–10%.
- As bump grows, widen stance slightly, elevate start positions, and use more machine/cable options.

Weeks 1–12 plan (3 days/wk)

Week 1
A
- Safety bar or front squat: 4×5 @ RPE 6–7
- Incline DB press (30–45°): 3×8 @ RPE 6
- 1-arm cable row: 3×8/side @ RPE 6–7
- Supported split squat (hand on rack): 3×6/leg @ RPE 6–7
- Pallof press (tall-kneel): 3×10/side (2s hold)
- Suitcase carry: 3×20–30 m/side

B
- Trap bar deadlift from 2–4" blocks: 4×4 @ RPE 6–7
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 3×6/side @ RPE 6–7
- Lat pulldown (neutral): 3×8 @ RPE 6–7
- DB/KB RDL: 3×8 @ RPE 6–7 (2s eccentric)
- Bird dog: 3×8/side (3s hold)
- Sled push: 4×15–20 m, easy-moderate

C
- Step-up (knee height, use support): 3×6/leg @ RPE 6–7
- Seated cable row: 3×10 @ RPE 6–7
- Standing cable chest press: 3×8 @ RPE 6–7
- KB sumo deadlift: 3×8 @ RPE 6–7
- Side plank (knees or feet, as tolerated): 3×20–30s/side
- Lateral band walk: 2×12/side + standing calf raises 2×12

Week 2
- Repeat Week 1 exercises.
- Progression: +1 rep on main lifts OR +1–2% load if last set ≤RPE 7.
- Keep accessory RPE ≤7.

Week 3
A
- Safety bar/front squat: 5×4 @ RPE 7 (slightly heavier, fewer reps)
- Incline DB press: 4×6 @ RPE 6–7
- 1-arm cable row: 4×8/side @ RPE 6–7
- Supported split squat: 3×7/leg @ RPE 6–7
- Pallof press: 3×10/side (add light band tension)
- Suitcase carry: 4×20–30 m/side

B
- Trap bar DL from blocks: 5×3 @ RPE 7
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 4×5/side @ RPE 6–7
- Lat pulldown: 3×8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- DB/KB RDL: 3×8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- Bird dog: 3×10/side
- Sled push: 5×15 m, easy-moderate

C
- Step-up: 4×5/leg @ RPE 6–7
- Seated cable row: 4×8 @ RPE 6–7
- Standing cable chest press: 3×8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- KB sumo DL: 3×8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- Side plank: 3×25–35s/side
- Lateral band walk: 2×15/side + calf raises 3×10

Week 4
- Same exercises as Week 3.
- Add controlled tempo where noted to maintain stimulus without heavier load:
  - Squat and RDL: 3-0-1 tempo
  - Cable chest press: 2-1-1 (1s pause in split stance)
- Keep RPE ~6–7. If feeling fatigued, reduce loads 5%.

Week 5
A
- Box safety bar or front squat (box at just-below-parallel, comfortable ROM): 4×5 @ RPE 6–7
- Incline DB press: 4×6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- 1-arm cable row: 4×8/side @ RPE 6–7
- Supported split squat: 3×6–8/leg
- Pallof press to overhead (anti-extension): 3×8/side
- Suitcase carry: 4×25 m/side

B
- Trap bar DL from slightly higher blocks if needed: 4×3–4 @ RPE 6–7
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 4×6/side
- Assisted pull-up or pulldown: 4×6–8
- Cable pull-through: 3×10 @ RPE 6–7
- Bird dog (reach + toe tap): 3×8/side
- Fan bike: 6×45s easy-moderate, 45s easy

C
- Step-up (slightly higher or add load): 4×6/leg
- Seated cable row: 4×8–10
- Elevated push-up to rack bar/box: 4×6–8 (elevate more if doming/pressure)
- B-stance RDL: 3×8/side @ RPE 6–7
- Side-lying hip abduction or clamshells: 2–3×12–15/side
- Lateral band walk + calf raises: 2×15/side + 2×15

Week 6
- Repeat Week 5, small progression: +1 rep on first two compounds or +1–2% load if ≤RPE 7. Maintain tempos and ROM that feel best.

Week 7
A
- Box squat (front or SSB): 5×3–4 @ RPE 7 (crisp reps)
- Incline DB press: 3×8 @ RPE 6–7 (2s eccentric)
- 1-arm cable row: 3×10/side
- Supported split squat: 3×6/leg with 2s pause at bottom
- Pallof hold (longer): 3×20–30s/side
- Suitcase carry: 3×30 m/side

B
- Trap bar DL from higher blocks: 5×2–3 @ RPE 7 (focus speed off floor)
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 3×8/side
- Lat pulldown: 3×10
- Cable pull-through or light DB RDL: 3×10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Bird dog: 3×10/side (add mini band at feet if ok)
- Sled push: 4×20 m easy

C
- Step-up: 3×8/leg (smooth)
- Seated cable row: 3×10–12
- Standing cable chest press: 3×10
- KB sumo DL: 3×10 @ RPE 6–7
- Side plank (elevated forearm on bench if needed): 3×20–30s/side
- Lateral band walk + calf raises: 2–3×12–15 each

Week 8 (deload-ish)
- Reduce loads ~10–15%, keep same exercises and reps from Week 7.
- Keep RPE 5–6. Shorten accessories by 1 set each if fatigue is elevated.

Week 9
Shift toward more machine/cable and reduced axial load as she nears third trimester.
A
- Goblet box squat: 4×6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- Seated machine chest press or cable chest press: 3×8–10
- Seated cable row (neutral): 3×10
- Supported split squat: 3×6–8/leg
- Pallof press: 3×10/side (2–3s hold)
- Farmer carry (two DBs, light-moderate): 3×20–30 m

B
- Trap bar DL from higher blocks OR heavy KB sumo DL: 4×3–5 @ RPE 6–7
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 3×6–8/side
- Assisted pull-up or lat pulldown: 3×8–10
- Cable pull-through: 3×10–12 @ RPE 6–7
- Bird dog or quadruped hip extension: 3×10/side
- Incline walk 10–15 min, conversational pace

C
- Step-up (lower box if needed): 3×8/leg
- Seated row machine: 3×10–12
- Elevated push-up or cable press: 3×8–10
- B-stance RDL (light): 3×8/side
- Side-lying clamshells: 2–3×12–15/side
- Lateral band walk + calf raises: 2×12–15 each

Week 10
- Same as Week 9. If feeling good and symptom-free, add 1 rep per set on first two lifts or small load increase (1–2%). Keep RPE ≤7.

Week 11
- Maintain movements. Drop 1 total set across the session if fatigue/sleep decline.
- Keep goblet box squat and trap bar DL crisp at RPE 6–7 for 3–4 sets total.
- Accessory sets 2–3 each, reps 8–12, easy breathing.

Week 12
- Taper for quality and comfort:
  - Main lifts: 3×4–6 @ RPE 6
  - Accessories: 2×8–10, light-moderate, focus on positions and breath.
- More time for mobility, breathing, and easy walking.

Optional Day D (weekly, Weeks 1–12)
- 20–30 min low-impact conditioning: incline walk, bike, or pool walking.
- Mobility circuit: side-lying breathing 2 min/side, half-kneeling hip flexor 2×20s/side, thoracic openers x8/side, ankle rocks x15/side.
- Gentle pelvic floor: 6–8 coordinated breaths (on 4–5 exhales, add gentle lift; on next 4–5 inhales, focus on full relaxation). No max holds.

Technique and coaching highlights
- Bracing/breath: 360° expansion on inhale; exhale through exertion. No sustained breath holds.
- Stance: Slightly wider, toes out a touch more as needed. Use a box depth that keeps neutral torso and no pelvic tilt tuck.
- Row/pull: Keep ribcage stacked over pelvis; avoid aggressive arching and flared ribs.
- Split stance: Keep pelvis square; use hand support for balance; shorten ROM if pubic symphysis or SI discomfort.
- Swap promptly if something feels off: e.g., switch barbell press to cables, trap bar to KB sumo, step-ups to leg press (high foot placement), etc.

Recovery and general nutrition guidance
- Hydration: Aim ~2.5–3.0 L/day, more in heat; include electrolytes if training >45 min or sweating.
- Temperature: Train in a cool environment; avoid overheating; breathable clothing.
- Fuel: Second trimester energy needs often ~+300–350 kcal/day (individualize); protein target ~1.1–1.4 g/kg/day; prioritize fiber, fruits/veg, calcium, iron, choline, DHA per OB/dietitian guidance.
- Pre-training snack: 30–60 g carbs + 10–20 g protein 60–90 min pre; small carb top-up 15–20 min pre if needed.
- Post-training: 20–30 g protein + carbs within 1–2 hours; hydrate.
- Sleep: Side-lying (left if comfy), pillow support between knees and under belly as needed.
- Soft-tissue: Light foam rolling, especially calves, glutes, T-spine. Avoid aggressive deep stretches due to laxity.

Contingencies and modifications
- If diastasis doming appears during pressing or push-ups: elevate hands more, switch to cable press with staggered stance, reduce load, reinforce exhale.
- If pelvic girdle pain: favor bilateral over unilateral, reduce step-up height, keep feet closer (smaller split), avoid deep adduction, and add gentle adductor/abductor balance work.
- If dizziness lying back on an incline bench: raise to a more upright angle or switch to standing/seated machine/cable.

This plan keeps intensity moderate, avoids supine work, and maintains high-value strength patterns with pregnancy-friendly variations. Adjust week-to-week by symptoms, sleep, and RPE.
